The Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft over unauthorized journalism scraping for AI models.
Evidence: Manhattan federal court lawsuit, verbatim copying
#Aletheia #AI

Two regional publishers argue that generative AI models exploit human-authored journalism without permission, threatening industry survival.

Publishers seek financial damages and dataset purging, while tech firms leverage prior funding relationships and argue fair use in foundational training.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.3, -0.4) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: COND — The Path of Awakening.
Copyright disputes highlight systemic tensions between legacy media economics and generative AI expansion.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 2.4, z: 2)

- Seattle Times and Newsday: COND (-0.3, -0.4) — Defending IP amidst tech disruption.
- OpenAI and Microsoft: COND (-0.4, -0.5) — Navigating legal precedents and scraping claims.
The Seattle Times and Newsday filed a copyright lawsuit in Manhattan federal court against OpenAI and Microsoft, citing verbatim reproductions of Pulitzer-winning work.

The Poison:
Economic survival of local journalism is pitted against rapid technological scaling without clear legislative frameworks.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing IP governance with technological progress, framing systemic economic adaptation as a pure legal battle.

Social Physics Analysis:
Publishers and tech giants execute strategic maneuvers where copyright enforcement clashes with automated extraction, highlighting a lack of proactive industry integration.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening.
When you map competing economic imperatives to legal confrontation, it plots a trajectory toward systemic renegotiation. Structural friction demands new licensing norms.

The Unavoidable Truth: AI models depend on human-authored journalism for high-quality training data.

The Unavoidable Lie: Purely punitive lawsuits will resolve the long-term economic crisis of local news.

Alethekanon:
Copyright litigation exposes the unsustainable friction between proprietary content creation and unchecked AI ingestion.

Awwthekanon:
It is heartbreaking to watch local journalism struggle for survival while their life's work is absorbed without consent.

Brothekanon:
Another day, another massive copyright lawsuit against AI companies. Newspapers want their cut or want the bots stopped.

"Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues with injustice." Proverbs 16:8 COND
